questions.question: What scalability contrast motivates combining recurrent networks with a generative model for time-series prediction?

options.A: A recurrent model's size depends on feature count rather than window length, whereas a joint-window generative predictor scales with both
options.B: A recurrent model scales with window length only, while diffusion scales with feature count only
options.C: Diffusion models require no context window, while recurrent models model the full joint density
options.D: Both model sizes are independent of feature dimension, but only the RNN scales with sequence length

questions.rationale: The paper says conventional recurrent model size is proportional to feature count, while generative predictors model a window whose dimensionality includes both features and temporal extent.
questions.evidence_quote: the model size is only proportional to the number of features, but not the length of the time window

questions.question: What data-distribution intuition leads the authors to initialize prediction from the current time point rather than Gaussian noise?

options.A: Neighboring time points are strongly correlated, so the future distribution is close to the current point's distribution
options.B: Future values are independent of the current observation, making a Gaussian prior exact
options.C: The context window is always Gaussian after RNN encoding
options.D: The current point has higher entropy than the future and is therefore easier to sample

questions.rationale: The authors reason that a nearby terminal distribution should ease transport learning, reduce inference complexity, and improve sample quality.
questions.evidence_quote:
Time series data is typically continuous and neighboring
time points exhibit strong correlations, indicating that the
distribution of future time points is close to that of the cur-
rent time point.

questions.question: What pair of time-series values does the proposed conditional SI module couple during training?

options.A: Adjacent observations xt and xt+1, conditioned on the history xt−P:t−1
options.B: The entire context window and an independent Gaussian vector, conditioned on the prediction horizon
options.C: Two randomly selected future observations, conditioned only on feature dimension
options.D: The first and last values of a sequence, without recurrent context

questions.rationale: The model learns the conditional joint of consecutive points given prior observations; the RNN summarizes that history as conditioning information.
questions.evidence_quote:
the generative model learns the joint distribution
p(xt+1, xt|xt−P :t−1) of the pair (xt+1, xt) given the past
observations xt−P :t−1.

questions.question: Why does the model encode history with an RNN instead of directly interpolating from the whole context window to the next point?

options.A: The stochastic interpolant endpoints must have the same sample-space size, so the RNN compresses history into a conditioning prompt
options.B: The SI score function accepts categorical inputs only, so continuous context cannot be used
options.C: The RNN is needed to make the endpoint distributions independent
options.D: The context window is missing during training and must be imputed first

questions.rationale: The paper notes the different vector sizes of full context and next-value target; an RNN converts the history into a fixed conditioning representation while SI transports xt to xt+1.
questions.evidence_quote: As the sample spaces of ρ0 and ρ1 must be the same, the generative model can not directly map the whole context window

questions.question: What sampling strategy addresses large loss contributions near the endpoints of the stochastic-interpolant time interval?

options.A: Importance-sample interpolation time from Beta(0.1, 0.1) and reweight by its proposal density
options.B: Sample interpolation time uniformly and remove all endpoint losses
options.C: Use a Gaussian proposal centered at 0.5 without importance weights
options.D: Set interpolation time to 0 or 1 with equal probability

questions.rationale: Algorithm 1 samples s from the Beta proposal and weights each loss contribution by the inverse sampling density to stabilize endpoint integration.

questions.question: Which model achieved the lowest CRPS-sum on the Wiki dataset, and what was its reported value?
questions.rationale: The SI Wiki score is the smallest among the Table 2 entries; lower CRPS-sum indicates better probabilistic forecasting.

questions.question: On which real-data forecasting dataset did Flow Matching outperform SI in CRPS-sum, and how did the paper qualify that result?

options.A: Traffic, 0.038±0.002 versus SI's 0.083±0.005, though FM performed extremely poorly on Wiki
options.B: Solar, 0.359±0.061 versus SI's 0.359±0.060, with no dataset-specific caveat
options.C: Exchange, 0.007±0.001 versus SI's 0.008±0.002, and FM was best everywhere
options.D: Wiki, 0.080±0.007 versus SI's 64.256±62.596, despite identical performance

questions.rationale: The table shows FM best on Traffic, but the text notes FM fails to capture Wiki's distribution and reports a huge Wiki CRPS-sum.
questions.evidence_quote: only on Traffic FM model achieves better performance.

questions.question: What comparison does the paper report between its SI framework and the recurrent Vec-LSTM baseline?

options.A: SI and other generative baselines outperform Vec-LSTM on all four listed datasets by CRPS-sum
options.B: Vec-LSTM outperforms SI on every dataset because it models temporal dependence directly
options.C: SI beats Vec-LSTM only on Exchange, while losing on Solar, Traffic, and Wiki
options.D: The methods tie on all datasets after normalizing CRPS-sum

questions.rationale: Each SI CRPS-sum entry is below the corresponding Vec-LSTM value; the authors attribute this to modeling the probability distribution more carefully.
questions.evidence_quote: By comparing to the RNN-based model Vec-LSTM, our model and other baselines such as SGM and DDPM get better performance

questions.question: How does inference produce forecasts beyond one future step in the proposed autoregressive setup?

options.A: Repeat the one-step conditional generation recursively, feeding each prediction into the next step
options.B: Sample the entire forecast horizon in one SI transport independent of prior outputs
options.C: Run the backward SDE from the final horizon to reconstruct all earlier context points
options.D: Use the RNN alone after the first SI-generated point

questions.rationale: The paper specifies recursive step-by-step prediction for multiple-step forecasting.
questions.evidence_quote: Regarding the multiple steps prediction, we recursively run the step-by-step prediction.
